newsitem.title: NIGER: President's allies take lead in Niger election.
newsitem.headline: President's allies take lead in Niger election.

text.p: The political party allied with Niger's president Ibrahim Bare Mainassara took an early lead in first results declared on Sunday from legislative elections marred by an opposition boycott.
The Independent Elections Committee put average turnout in voting on Saturday at 27.32 percent, confriming the impact of a boycott by the main opposition over a July presidential poll.
The opposition hailed the success of the boycott. Final turnout in July was 66.34 percent.

The Union of Independents for Democratic Renewal won 26 seats from 39 declared by midday. Five went to the ANDP party and the rest were shared by independents and minor parties, the committee said in a statement.
The main opposition parties are demanding a rerun of the chaotic presidential election they say was rigged by Mainassara.
Political problems since the start of a democartic transition in 1990 have stoked economic decline in one of the poorest countries in Sub-Saharan Africa.
A series a strikes over the past year linked to the political crisis spread at some point to Niger's lifeblood uranium mining industry, already depressed by low world prices.

A total of 220 candidates from around a dozen small parties vied for for the 83-seat assembly. The committee said the results declared were from 2,620 of a total 8,300 polling stations nationwide. Around 3.8 million people were eligible to vote.
Mainassara, a coupmaker who legalised his rule through the disputed July election, had urged a huge turnout and expressed regret that the opposition was not taking part.
"The low turnout shows Niger cannot be governed without the opposition," leading opposition politician Bello Tiousso Garba told Reuters.
Mainassara ousted the elected government of civilian president Mahamane Ousmane in a coup last January following a long standoff between Ousmane and his prime minister.

The general offered himself for election in July, but then suspended the electoral commission on the second day of polling, accusing it of irregularities, and placed his opponents under house arrest. He appointed a new commission which declared him winner with 52.22 percent of votes cast.
The United States said the election was fraudulent and suspended development aid.
Opposition politicians, including Ousmane, refused to register for Saturday's poll demanding that the result of the July presidential election be scrapped.
Final provisonal results were expected sometime on Sunday but these would have to be verified by the Supreme Court.
